item.title: NETEX continues discussions for long-term lease agreement with TNW
item.description: The Northeast Texas Rural Rail Transportation (NETEX) District board discussed a long-term lease agreement with TNW Corporation, the Northeast Texas Transportation Summit, membership to the Texas Short Line and Regional Railroad Association, a possible injury claim, payment ratifications and updates regarding a HASA agreement at their regularly scheduled board meeting on Thursday, March 5.

item.title: Como-Pickton celebrates FFA Week with year’s highlights
item.description: National Future Farmers of America Week was celebrated the last week of February, but due to the busy schedules surrounding the Northeast Texas Livestock Association’s Hopkins County Junior Market Livestock Show, Como-Pickton has decided to have a personal FFA week from March 9-13.The Como-Pickton High School FFA officers presented updates regarding their chapter during the Como-Pickton Consolidated Independent School District school board meeting on Monday, March 9.

item.title: Lady Bears lose two games to Wolfe City
item.description: WOLFE CITY — The Sulphur Bluff Lady Bears suffered a pair of losses in a doubleheader against the Wolfe City Lady Wolves March 10. In both games, the Lady Bears struggled on both sides of the ball and weren’t able to establish any rhythm, losing by scores of 17-1 and 18-2.

item.title: Trojans drop pair of games vs. Alba-Golden
item.description: FRUITVALE — The Cumby Trojans began their district schedule Monday, taking on the Alba-Golden Panthers in a doubleheader at Fruitvale High School. Unfortunately, the Trojans suffered losses in both games, losing 12-10 and 16-7.

item.title: An evening with local author Michael Johnson
item.description: Campbell author, humorist and playwright Michael Johnson gave a speech titled “What Is It that Helps Us?” at the Main Street Theatre Saturday, March 14. Johnson is an author of 10 different books, including titles such as “The Story of Blue, A Rope Horse” and “The Trials of Joe Ben Black, Confessions of a Rope Horse,” which were available for purchase at Main Street Theatre on Saturday.

item.title: 25% of Carter BloodCare’s blood supply comes from high school blood drives
item.description: About 25% of Carter BloodCare’s blood supply comes from high school blood drives. When student donors leave for spring break, that steady stream of donations pauses almost overnight. But hospital demand does not.

item.title: Residents speak out against request to rezone Booker Street property
item.description: Nearly a dozen Sulphur Springs residents spoke in opposition to a requestto change a Booker Street property from single family to multifamily zoning during Monday night’s Planning & Zoning Commission meeting; a proposed amendment to the City of Sulphur Springs’ policies regarding where tattoo and body piercing establishments and certain parking requirements were also discussed at the meeting.

item.title: New playground equipment installed at North Hopkins ISD
item.description: North Hopkins Independent School District welcomed a new piece of playground equipment on the elementary campus Friday, March 13. Superintendent Brian Lowe revealed this during his reports at the school board meeting on Thursday, Feb. 26, along with discussing plans for the calendar, bus updates, field house updates and administration contract extensions.

item.title: April 11 Kerry W. Garmon Memorial Educational Foundation Sholarship Dinner, Auction benefits Saltillo seniors
item.description: The Kerry W. Garmon Memorial Educational Foundation’s Annual Dinner and Auction is scheduled to begin at 6 p.m.

item.title: HWGC: Construction for two new SSISD elementary campuses still on schedule
item.description: Representatives from Hill & Wilkinson General Contractors report construction for the new Sulphur Springs and Rowena Johnson Elementary Schools was still on schedule at the Sulphur Springs Independent School District board meeting on Monday, March 16.
